sources.matrix: own transitions (14.0, weighted by the HMM's regime probabilities) + the panel's HMM matrix (1061 companies, 12188 company-years) at K = 6
sources.regimes: hidden Markov model of yearly growth, pooled over 1061 companies (12188 company-years, annual XBRL frames since 2010): regimes average +29.0%, +8.8%, +3.8%
sources.now: the HMM's probability of each regime in the latest year: 1% / 29% / 70%
sources.growth: the HMM's regime means and spreads (2699/4974/4515 company-years per regime); spreads × 1.5, fitted in the walk-forward backtest so that the 80% range of revenue three years out holds about 80% of what happened (as estimated, the spreads made it too narrow)
sources.years_1_2: no consensus with ≥ 3 analysts: the regime model from year 1
sources.margin: trailing EBIT margin 9.0%; regime drift = panel median; κ = 0.20 (pooled regression, 8802 pairs)
sources.sbc: already a cost inside GAAP operating income, so counted once (not added back, not deducted again)
sources.wacc: the company WACC above (Treasury + Blume beta × ERP, bond-calibrated cost of debt)

backtest.text: Backtest (run in 2013–2019 on every filer's data as of then, 2,274 outcomes, without analysts' consensus): the 80% range of revenue three years out held 80% of what happened (11% fell below it, 9% above) — about right. That is with every regime's growth spread × 1.5, the one number fitted on these outcomes (and used here): as the hidden Markov model estimates them, the range held 68% (18% below, 14% above) — a single year's regime spread understates how far revenue can drift over several.
